import re def detect_html_tags(html_str: str) -> list[str]: """ Detect all HTML tags in the provided string using a regular expression. Parameters ---------- html_str : str The input string containing HTML content to be analyzed. Returns ------- list[str] A list of strings, each representing an HTML tag found in the input. The tags include both opening and closing forms, e.g. '
', ''. Notes ----- - The function is intentionally tolerant: it will not raise an exception on malformed input or unexpected data types. In such cases, it simply returns an empty list. - The regex pattern is designed to capture any substring that starts with '<', contains any characters except '>' (non-greedy), and ends with '>'. """ try: # Regex to capture tags: starts with <, followed by any characters except >, # and ends with >. The pattern is non-greedy to avoid overmatching. tag_pattern = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>", re.IGNORECASE) return tag_pattern.findall(html_str or "") except Exception: # If anything goes wrong (e.g., invalid regex compilation, type errors), # return an empty list instead of raising. return []
